transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi, thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I really appreciate it. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time. It's probably just normal stress, you know? But things have just been a little overwhelming lately. 

I work in a chemistry lab—I'm still trying to finish my degree—and lately, my mind is just constantly jumping around. Like, I can't stop thinking about whether our lab's new partnership is going to end up cutting my position, or... or if all my recent data is just completely wrong. And then from there, I start stressing about my bills piling up, and how my family probably thinks I'm falling behind everyone else... and whether I've just already ruined my chances at ever getting into grad school. 

I just... I worry about all of it, all at once, almost all the time. Is... is that normal for someone my age? I hope I'm explaining this okay.
Do you find that your worrying is something you can’t seem to control or turn off, even when you try?

Well, I really do try to turn it off. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting there letting it happen, or that I'm not trying my best to work. I'll tell myself to just... just focus on one single task, you know? Like finishing a lab report or, um, checking an assay. 

But then it's like one little worry just sets off another one, and... pretty soon I'm just staring blankly at the screen. My head just starts running through every possible way things could go wrong, even when I'm trying so hard to push it away. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be better at managing my thoughts by now. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping, that seem to go along with all this worrying?

Well, I... I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I'm sure everyone gets a little on edge sometimes, right? But, um, yeah, I guess I do get a bit... wound up. 

Especially at work. It's like I just can't seem to settle into my chair. I try to look busy and professional, but I catch myself tapping my foot constantly, or... or checking my messages over and over. Sometimes I'll even just walk back to the instrument room for no real reason, just because I feel like I need to be moving. And, um, I've noticed I get startled really easily lately. Like, just normal lab noises—a centrifuge finishing or someone dropping a pipette box—and I'll jump. 

I know it probably looks really unprofessional, and I'm trying to keep it under wraps so my supervisor doesn't think I'm slacking off. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting to just normal stress.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still care about all those things! I definitely don't want you to think I'm just giving up or, you know, getting lazy about my life. 

I still really want to do well at work and finish my degree, and I still love hanging out with my friends. It's just... sometimes it's hard to be fully present when we're together, because my brain is still running through all those worries I mentioned. But I still want to be there! I haven't lost interest at all. I still try to keep up with everything. 

Is that... is that a good sign? I hope it means things aren't too bad.
Do these feelings of constant worry and physical tension happen most days, or are they more tied to specific stressful events?

Um, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of the exact days or anything. I definitely don't want to exaggerate and say it's happening all the time, because I know I have good days where I'm just getting my work done and being productive! I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about normal life. 

But, um, I haven't really noticed if it's tied to specific stressful events, either. I guess I just haven't been paying close enough attention to a pattern. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. I should probably be keeping a log or something, right? I usually just try to put my head down and push through it so I don't fall behind on my projects. 

Is it okay that I don't have a clear answer for that? I can try to start tracking it for you if that's what I'm supposed to do.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these worries and physical symptoms been happening pretty consistently for several months, or have they come on more recently?

Um, well, I guess it's been... maybe around seven months? Give or take? I don't want to make it sound like I've been struggling forever, because I really have been trying to handle it. 

It kind of started when the lab went through this big funding shift, and we got this new commercial partnership. It just changed how everything was being run, and the expectations shifted, so... I guess that's when I started feeling more on edge. But I mean, anyone would feel a little stressed with a big change like that at work, right? It's totally normal to need an adjustment period. 

I just... I hope I haven't let it go on too long before talking to someone. Is seven months a really long time to be dealing with this? I really have been trying my best to just adapt and keep up with the new workflow.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed lately, especially when you're feeling overwhelmed by these worries?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I've been irritable or anything like that. I really try hard not to take my stress out on other people, especially at the lab. We all have a lot on our plates right now, so it wouldn't be fair for me to get snappy just because I'm feeling a little overwhelmed, you know? 

I mean, maybe I get a tiny bit quieter if I'm really focused on trying to get a reaction set up right while my brain is buzzing, but I'm definitely not snapping at anyone or getting angry. I try to be really easy to work with. 

I hope that's okay? Like, it's a good thing that I'm not getting angry at people, right? I just want to make sure I'm handling things the right way.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things in your life, not just the changes at work?

Um, I mean... I guess it does kind of spill over into other things. I don't want to sound like I'm just worrying about absolutely everything, because I know I have a lot to be grateful for, and I really try to keep things in perspective. 

But, um, yeah, it's not just the lab partnership and whether they're going to cut my position. My brain kind of just... jumps around a lot. Like, I'll start worrying that my data is completely wrong, and then that spirals into worrying about whether I've already completely ruined my chances of getting into grad school. And then I start thinking about my bills piling up, and if my family thinks I'm just falling behind everyone else my age. 

I know it probably sounds silly to worry about all of that at once. I really try not to let it get to me, and I know everyone has financial stuff and family stuff to think about. It's totally normal to care about your future, right? I just... I hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm totally falling apart. I'm still getting my work done! Is it normal for work stress to kind of trigger worries about other stuff like that?
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

Um, well, I guess I have been... a little tired? But I really don't want to sound lazy or like I'm just making excuses. I know everyone works hard and gets tired, so I try not to complain about it. 

It's just... even when I spend a full night in bed, I wake up feeling like I've already pulled an all-nighter. I really try to push through it and keep a good attitude, but by the time I'm at work labeling samples, or even just trying to cook dinner for my family later on, my body just feels so heavy. And my brain feels completely drained. 

I'm still getting all my work done, though! I promise I'm not slacking off or anything. It's just taking a lot more effort lately. Is it normal to feel that exhausted when I'm just doing lab work and not, like, heavy physical labor? I just want to make sure I'm not blowing it out of proportion.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks because your mind is so caught up in worrying?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little bit? But I really try my best to stay focused, especially at the lab. I know how important it is to be precise with the materials and the data, so I double-check everything I do. I definitely don't want you to think I'm messing up at work or anything like that. 

Sometimes, though, it's just... my mind kind of drifts a bit to those other things we talked about, like grad school or the bills. But as soon as I catch myself, I snap right back to what I'm doing. I think everyone probably daydreams or gets a little distracted sometimes, right? 

I'm really trying hard to keep my mind on track. I haven't made any big mistakes or anything. That's a good sign, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
Do you find that this tiredness or low energy is worse when you're not doing things you enjoy, or does it seem to hang around even when you're doing activities that usually make you feel good?

Um... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I really try to stay positive and enjoy the things I usually like doing, you know? Like hanging out with my family or just watching a movie. I don't want to be a downer for anyone else.

But... I guess even when I'm trying to relax and do fun stuff, that heavy, drained feeling is still kind of there in the background. It's not like I'm completely miserable or anything! I still smile and try to have a good time. I just... I don't always have the same bounce in my step, I suppose. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for the good things in my life. I know it's important to appreciate the fun moments. Is it normal to still feel that tired even when you're supposed to be having fun? I'm trying my best to push past it, I really am.

When you're feeling especially overwhelmed, does your worry feel like it's specifically tied to the stress of changes at work, or does it seem to go beyond those stressors and come up even when things are relatively calm?

Um, gosh, I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I guess I haven't really noticed a clear pattern? 

I definitely don't want to make it sound like my job is too much for me. I can handle the lab work and the changes, I promise. I'm really grateful for my position, so I try not to complain when things get a little hectic there. 

But as for whether the worry happens when things are calm... I don't know, maybe? It kind of all just blends together for me. Like, even if I'm just sitting at home on the couch and nothing is really going on, my mind might still be going over things. But I always just figured that was normal, you know? Like my brain is just being thorough and making sure I didn't forget anything important for my family or for work. 

I try really hard to just go with the flow and stay relaxed when I'm supposed to be. I hope it's okay that I don't have a more specific answer for you. I just haven't really tracked it that closely, I guess. Does that make sense?
Do you find that you still feel this level of worry even during times when there isn’t anything specific or stressful happening in your life?

Um, well... I guess I'm honestly not too sure? I really try my best to just enjoy the quiet days when there isn't anything big going on. I definitely don't want to be the kind of person who just looks for things to stress about when everything is actually totally fine, you know? 

I mean, maybe my mind still races a little bit during those times, but I haven't really paid close enough attention to say if it's the exact same level of worry. I just try to keep a positive attitude about it all and stay productive. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a better answer for you on that one... I just really haven't noticed a clear difference. Am I doing okay with these questions? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you find that your anxiety or worry tends to show up even on days when nothing particularly stressful or challenging is happening?

Um... I feel like you might have asked me this just a minute ago, or something similar? I'm sorry if my last answer wasn't very clear. I really want to be helpful here.

Like I said, I'm honestly not entirely sure. I try really hard to just relax on days when there's nothing going on. I don't want to be someone who just makes up things to worry about when everything is perfectly fine. 

I guess... maybe my brain is still kind of buzzing in the background even on quiet days? But I really try to just push past it and focus on the good things. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I'm trying my best to explain it right.
Can you tell me if you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even on days when nothing out of the ordinary is happening?

Um... I'm really sorry, doctor, but I think... I think we're going in circles a little bit? I feel terrible, I must not be explaining myself very well at all if you have to keep asking the same thing. I'm really trying, I promise.

I just... I don't know how else to say it. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around looking for problems when it's a normal, quiet day. I really try to be grateful and just, you know, enjoy the peace. If I feel a little tense, I just tell myself it's nothing and try to stay busy. 

I'm so sorry I can't give you a simple yes or no. I just don't want to give you the wrong impression of how I handle things. Is... is it okay that I'm struggling with this question? I really don't want to frustrate you.
Can you recall any recent days when nothing particularly stressful or unusual was happening, and if so, did you still feel anxious or worried on those days?

Um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm really letting you down here. I know you're trying to get a specific answer from me, and I'm just... I'm really struggling to give you what you need. I feel awful that we're still stuck on this. 

I guess... if I think about last weekend, for example. I didn't have to go into the lab, I didn't have any classes to worry about, it was just a normal Saturday. And... well, I suppose I did still feel kind of on edge? Like, my chest was a little tight and I couldn't quite settle down to just watch a movie or anything. 

But I really tried not to let it bother me! I just got up and cleaned the apartment and tried to be productive instead of just sitting there worrying about nothing. I know it's silly to be anxious when there's no reason for it, so I really try to just push through it. 

I hope that helps a little bit more? I'm so sorry for being difficult, I really am trying my best to be a good patient for you.
Can you tell me if you tend to feel anxious or worried on most days, even when there isn’t anything specific causing stress at that time?

Um... I know we keep coming back to this, and I'm really sorry if I haven't been answering it right. I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. I'm usually really good at holding it together.

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, yeah. Most days are like that. It's actually kind of why I came in to see you. I just... my mind doesn't really stop? It's always jumping around to different things. Like, one minute I'm terrified that our lab's new partnership is going to mean my position gets cut, and then I'm obsessing over whether my data is wrong, or if my bills are going to pile up. 

And then it just spirals into worrying that my family thinks I'm falling behind everyone else, or that I've already completely ruined my chances at getting into grad school. It just... it plays on a loop in my head, even when I'm just sitting at home trying to eat dinner. 

I know it sounds like I'm overreacting to everything, and I really try not to let it show at work. I hope you don't think I'm just being dramatic? I just... I can't seem to turn it off, no matter how hard I try. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
